attachments.origin_landmark: adductor part: inferior pubic ramus + ischial ramus; hamstring (ischiocondylar) part: ischial tuberosity
attachments.insertion_landmark: adductor part: linea aspera (broad linear insertion); hamstring part: adductor tubercle (via a distinct tendon, with a hiatus for the femoral vessels between the two)

functional_compartments.name: Adductor part

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: along the linear central tendon -- for where this band lies along the muscle, see motor_endplate_zones

functional_compartments.function_note: Embryologically/functionally an adductor-group muscle, obturator-nerve innervated.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset; Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

motor_endplate_zones.notes: Corresponds to the middle third of the thigh. Reported by the source for the muscle as a whole; this atlas's functional compartments are not separately mapped there, so the same zone is recorded on each.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites

functional_compartments.name: Hamstring (ischiocondylar) part

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: mid-belly endplate band -- for where this band lies along the muscle, see motor_endplate_zones

functional_compartments.function_note: Functionally behaves as a 4th hamstring (hip extensor), sciatic-nerve innervated -- the textbook example of a single named muscle with two developmentally/functionally distinct, separately-innervated compartments.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset; Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

motor_endplate_zones.notes: Corresponds to the middle third of the thigh. Reported by the source for the muscle as a whole; this atlas's functional compartments are not separately mapped there, so the same zone is recorded on each.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the middle third of the medial thigh, with the limb supine and the hip abducted, externally rotated and semi-flexed and the knee semi-flexed.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deep to gracilis, lying directly on the femoral cortex.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: The same non-standard position as for gracilis. In cerebral palsy, injection significantly reduces spasticity and helps prevent hip dislocation; after total hip arthroplasty it has reduced pain on the visual analogue scale and improved gait during rehabilitation.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites
